guides.title: AI for school and college students in India
guides.summary: Use free AI apps as a patient tutor for board exams and college work, in your own language. Know where the official free study material is, and how to use AI without copying.

body: A free AI chat app can be a tutor that never gets tired of your questions. ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot and Meta AI in WhatsApp can all explain a topic, test you and check your working. Google says India is the top country for Guided Learning, the study feature in Gemini, and that Gemini works in 10 Indian languages. So you can ask in your own language, or in a mix with English, and ask again until the idea is clear.

Check the age rules first. ChatGPT is not meant for children under 13, and those aged 13 to 18 need a parent's permission. Gemini needs you to be 13 or older, or the age set for your country. Claude is only for people aged 18 and above. If you are old enough, turn on the study feature: "Study and learn" in ChatGPT, or Guided Learning in Gemini. These give hints and questions step by step, so you do the thinking yourself.

Use AI with your board syllabus, not in place of it. Tell the app your board, class, subject and chapter. Ask it to explain, then to test you. CBSE puts sample question papers and marking schemes for Classes 10 and 12 on cbseacademic.nic.in, so check your answers against those and your textbook. From 2026, CBSE Class 10 students can also sit a second, optional board exam in May to improve up to three subjects, and the better score counts.

You do not need to pay for good study material. DIKSHA (diksha.gov.in) has textbooks, videos and practice questions for NCERT, CBSE, NIOS and state boards, up to Class 12. SWAYAM (swayam.gov.in) has more than 4,400 free courses from NPTEL, IGNOU, NCERT, NIOS and others; you pay only if you want the exam certificate. SWAYAM Prabha runs 48 free education TV channels on DD Free Dish. If AI says something different from these, trust your textbook and ask your teacher.

Copying from AI is not learning, and it can lead to punishment. In 2023 CBSE said that using ChatGPT in a board exam counts as unfair means, and phones and other devices are not allowed in the exam hall. For college assignments there was still no single UGC rule in April 2026, so each college sets its own. Shiv Nadar University asks students to declare how they used AI, and teachers at Delhi University and NLSIU Bengaluru have added viva questions.

AI can be wrong and still sound sure. It can give a wrong formula, a wrong date or the name of a book that does not exist. Check every fact in your NCERT or board textbook. Do not type your full name, school, address, phone number, Aadhaar number or passwords into a chatbot. Do not believe or forward messages that offer a leaked board paper. If exam stress feels too heavy, talk to a parent, teacher or school counsellor, not only to an app.
tips: Type: "I am in Class 10, CBSE. Explain how a convex lens forms an image, in simple Hindi and English. Then ask me 5 questions, one at a time."
Turn on "Study and learn" in ChatGPT or Guided Learning in Gemini to get hints and questions, not ready answers.
Solve a sum yourself first, then type: "Here is my working. Find my mistake, but do not give me the full answer."
Type: "Make a 30-day revision timetable for Class 12 Physics, Chemistry and Maths. I have 3 hours a day. Keep one rest day each week."
Paste your own essay and type: "Point out grammar mistakes and unclear lines. Do not rewrite it for me."
Before a college assignment, read your college's rule on AI or ask your teacher, and add one line saying how you used AI.
Check every answer against your textbook and the official sample paper marking scheme.
Never type your full name, school name, phone number, Aadhaar number or passwords into a chatbot.

guides.title: AI for competitive exam aspirants
guides.summary: Use AI to plan your study, clear doubts, practise questions and get feedback for JEE, NEET, CUET, UPSC, SSC, bank, railway and state PSC exams. Know what to check against official sources.

stats.label: candidates appeared in JEE Main 2026 Session 1
stats.source: National Testing Agency figures reported by Careers360, 16 February 2026

stats.label: candidates wrote the UPSC civil services prelims in 2026, for 933 civil services posts
stats.source: News On AIR (Akashvani), 27 May 2026

body: Lakhs of people sit each big exam. About 13.04 lakh appeared in JEE Main 2026 Session 1, and nearly 5.49 lakh wrote the UPSC civil services prelims in 2026 for 933 posts. Many aspirants study alone, far from the big coaching cities. A free AI chat app can help you plan, explain a hard concept late at night and set practice questions. ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot and others can all do this. Treat it as a study partner that is sometimes wrong.

Begin with a plan. Tell the AI your exam, the exam date, the hours you have each day and your weak subjects. Ask for a week-by-week timetable with revision and mock test days. Paste the official syllabus so it does not add or drop topics. For a hard concept, ask for a simple explanation, then a harder one, then five questions. If you studied in Hindi or another language, ask it to explain in that language and give the English terms too.

Use AI for practice, but check answers with official keys. Ask for questions in your exam's pattern and solve them with a timer. Then compare with real past papers. NTA puts out provisional answer keys, and for NEET UG 2026 candidates could challenge an answer for ₹200 per question. In May 2026 UPSC released a provisional answer key for the civil services prelims for the first time. When the AI and the official key differ, follow the official key.

Free official help exists. SATHEE (sathee.iitk.ac.in), from the Ministry of Education and IIT Kanpur, gives free lectures, mock tests and more than 80,000 questions for JEE, NEET, CUET, SSC, bank (IBPS) and railway (RRB) exams, in Hindi, English and other languages. It also runs on seven DTH TV channels. Some AI apps now have full mock tests too: Gemini offers JEE Main and NEET UG practice tests, and the NEET questions are made with PhysicsWallah and Careers360.

For UPSC, state PSC and bank descriptive papers, write your answer by hand first. Then type it in and ask the AI to mark it like a strict examiner: structure, missing points and word limit. For current affairs, paste a report from an official source such as News On AIR (newsonair.gov.in) and ask for a short summary and likely questions. Before an interview, ask the AI to act as a board member and ask about your home district, degree and hobbies. Say your answers aloud.

Know the limits. AI can give wrong facts, old syllabus points and invented "previous year questions". Check with NCERT books and the official syllabus on sites such as nta.ac.in and upsc.gov.in. Never pay for a "leaked paper". NEET UG held in May 2026 was cancelled after leak allegations. Before the June re-exam, NTA said there was no leaked paper, while scammers on Telegram asked ₹14,000 to 25,000 for one. A stricter 2026 law sets up to 10 years in jail and fines up to ₹10 crore.
tips: Type: "I am preparing for an SSC exam in 4 months. I can study 3 hours on weekdays and 6 hours on Sunday. Make a weekly plan with revision and mock test days."
Type: "Explain rotational motion as you would to a Class 11 student, in Hindi with the English terms. Then give me 5 MCQs."
Paste the official syllabus and type: "Use only this syllabus. Which topics from it are missing in my notes below?"
In Gemini, type "I want to take a NEET mock exam" for a full practice test in English; you can ask for a JEE Main mock test in the same way.
After a mock test, type: "These are the questions I got wrong. Group my mistakes by topic and tell me what to revise first."
Type: "Mark this answer out of 10 like a strict examiner. List the missing points. Do not rewrite it."
Type: "Act as an interview board for a bank officer post. Ask one question at a time and wait for my answer."
Check each AI answer against the official answer key or your NCERT book before you write it in your notes.

guides.title: AI for freshers and job seekers in India
guides.summary: Use AI to write a clear CV, practise interviews in English and choose skills to learn. Find the official free job and apprenticeship portals, and learn to spot fake job offers.

stats.label: jobseekers registered on the National Career Service portal (shown as 69.2 million)
stats.source: National Career Service, Ministry of Labour and Employment, home page, November 2026

stats.label: active vacancies on the National Career Service portal on 30 April 2026
stats.source: Directorate General of Employment, NCS E-Newsletter, April 2026

stats.label: fee charged by the National Career Service for registration, job applications or interviews

body: Finding a first job takes many applications and a lot of waiting. A free AI chat app can help at each step. ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot and Meta AI can all draft, correct and ask practice questions. Use it like a helpful senior who reads your CV and gives honest comments. But the facts must come from you. AI does not know your marks, your project or your internship, and if you let it guess, it will write things that are not true.

For a CV, type your real details in plain words: degree, college, year, marks, projects, internship and skills. Paste the job advert and ask for a one-page fresher CV that matches it. Then ask which skills in the advert you have not shown. For a cover letter or email, ask for about 120 words and add one true example from your own life. The Government's National Career Service portal also lists an AI resume builder among its services.

Many freshers fear the English interview more than the questions. Practise with AI, by voice or by typing. Ask it to act as an HR interviewer for the exact job, to ask one question at a time, and to correct your English gently after each answer. Ask for a simple five-line answer to "Tell me about yourself", then say it aloud until it sounds natural. Ask it to explain any hard word in Hindi or your own language.

Search on official portals. The National Career Service (ncs.gov.in), run by the Ministry of Labour and Employment, lists jobs, job fairs, internships and career counselling, and shows about 6.9 crore registered jobseekers. It charges no fee at any stage, and its toll-free helpline is 1514. For apprenticeships, where you learn on the job and get a monthly stipend, see apprenticeshipindia.gov.in and the National Apprenticeship Training Scheme at nats.education.gov.in. Sign up only on the official sites.

Ask AI what to learn next. Paste three job adverts you like and ask which skills appear in all of them. Then ask for a four-week plan that uses free courses. The Skill India Digital Hub (skillindiadigital.gov.in) has courses in AI and digital skills, and it is now linked with the National Career Service. The Government's YUVA AI for All course is free, takes a little over four hours and gives a Government of India certificate.

Stay safe. Fake job offers are common, and AI cannot tell you if an offer is real. The Department of Telecommunications lists two warning signs: a request for money or bank details, and emails from free, non-official addresses. In May 2026 the Home Ministry's cybercrime centre warned about fake online interviews that scan your face or eyes. Never pay a fee, and never hand over a bank passbook, card, SIM, Aadhaar details or OTP. Report fraud on 1930 or at cybercrime.gov.in.
tips: Type: "Here are my details: [degree, college, year, marks, projects, skills]. Write a one-page fresher CV for this job advert: [paste advert]. Do not add anything I have not given you."
Type: "Act as an HR interviewer for a junior accountant post. Ask one question at a time. After each answer, correct my English and suggest a better answer."
Type: "Give me a simple 5-line answer to 'Tell me about yourself' for a B.Com fresher applying for an accounts job."
Type: "Write a polite 100-word email to HR asking about the status of my application sent on [date]."
Paste three job adverts and type: "Which skills appear in all three? Make a 4-week learning plan for me using free courses."
Remove your phone number, home address and Aadhaar number before you paste your CV into an AI app.
Read every line the AI writes and delete any skill, job or mark that is not true.
Register free on ncs.gov.in; if anyone asks for a registration fee or a security deposit for a job, stop and call 1930.

guides.title: AI for kirana shops and small businesses
guides.summary: Write WhatsApp messages, catalogue lines and customer replies faster, and keep simple accounts and stock lists. Learn where to register and sell online, and how to avoid payment and GST scams.

stats.label: enterprises registered on the Udyam and Udyam Assist portals, as shown on 25 November 2026
stats.source: Ministry of MSME, Udyam Registration portal dashboard, November 2026

stats.label: UPI payments made in October 2026, worth ₹31.53 lakh crore
stats.source: NPCI figures reported by Free Press Journal, 2 November 2026

stats.label: of orders on the Government e Marketplace (GeM) in 2025-26 went to micro and small enterprises
stats.source: News On AIR (Akashvani), 6 April 2026

body: Running a kirana shop, a tailoring unit or a repair service means doing ten jobs yourself. A free AI chat app can take over some of the writing and counting work. ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot and Meta AI in WhatsApp can all draft messages, product details and simple lists in minutes, in English, Hindi or your own language. You can type or speak. You must still check every price, date and promise, because the customer will hold you to it, not the app.

Start with customer messages. Tell the AI your shop name, the offer, the dates and the language. Ask for three short WhatsApp messages and pick the one that sounds like you. For a catalogue in the WhatsApp Business app, give the real facts of each item, such as size, material, weight and price, and ask for a two-line description. Take photos in daylight against a plain wall. Ask for a polite reply to a late-delivery complaint or a request for credit, then add your own words.

AI can also answer customers for you. In May 2026 Meta launched Business AI inside the WhatsApp Business app for eligible small businesses in India. It replies to common questions at any hour, using your business profile and catalogue, and Meta says it works in Indian languages. You can step in, change how it behaves or switch it off. Test it first from a friend's number. A wrong price or stock answer will upset a customer, so keep your catalogue up to date.

For accounts, type or speak the day's sales and expenses and ask for a table with totals. Ask for a stock list that shows which items are running low. Check every total with a calculator. AI can explain GST words such as HSN code, input tax credit or composition scheme in simple Hindi. Since 1 November 2025, small low-risk applicants can get GST registration within three working days. But rates and rules change, so ask a CA or GST practitioner before you file returns or print bills.

Three official platforms can widen your market. Udyam registration (udyamregistration.gov.in) is free, paperless and based on your own declaration; over 10 crore enterprises are on Udyam and Udyam Assist. ONDC, a Government-backed open network for online selling, crossed 50 crore transactions in July 2026. On GeM, where government offices buy, small enterprises won 68% of orders in 2025-26. UPI handled 2,547 crore payments in October 2026. To learn the basics of AI, the Government's free YUVA AI for All course takes about four hours.

Stay careful. Do not hand over goods on a payment screenshot. In September 2026 a shop in Kerala lost silver worth ₹16,000 to a fake Google Pay screen; check your own bank app, SMS or voice alert speaker. In January 2026 the tax department (CBIC) warned of fake GST notices; a real one carries a document number (DIN) that you can verify on the CBIC website. Do not paste customers' names or numbers into public AI apps. India's data protection law has penalties of up to ₹250 crore.
tips: Type: "Write 3 short WhatsApp messages in Hindi and English for my kirana shop, [shop name]. Offer: 5% off on monthly ration orders above ₹2,000, till 30 November. Keep it friendly."
Type: "Write a 2-line description for my WhatsApp catalogue: steel tiffin box, 3 containers, 750 ml, ₹320. Do not add any claim I have not given."
Type: "A customer says her order came two days late. Write a polite reply in simple Hindi. Say sorry, give this reason: [your reason], and offer free delivery next time."
Say: "Today's sales were [list]. Today's expenses were [list]. Make a table with totals and tell me today's profit." Then check the totals with a calculator.
Type: "Explain input tax credit in simple Hindi with one example from a kirana shop." Then confirm with your CA before you file.
Register on Udyam only at udyamregistration.gov.in. It is free, and no agent or other website is authorised to do it.
Before the customer leaves, check the payment in your own bank or UPI app, not on the customer's phone.
Replace customer names and phone numbers with "Customer 1", "Customer 2" before you paste a list into an AI app.

guides.title: AI for farmers in India
guides.summary: Use your phone, by photo or by voice in your own language, to check a crop problem, the weather, mandi prices and government schemes. Know which official tools to trust and where AI can go wrong.

stats.label: farmer questions answered by the Kisan e-Mitra voice chatbot by December 2025
stats.source: Press Information Bureau (PIB Research), AI in agriculture note, 14 February 2026

stats.label: mandis linked to the eNAM online market by March 2026, with 1.80 crore farmers registered
stats.source: Press Information Bureau (PIB Research), e-NAM note, 13 April 2026

stats.label: pests across 66 crops covered by the National Pest Surveillance System in December 2025
stats.source: Press Information Bureau (PIB Research), AI in agriculture note, 14 February 2026

body: Pests, weather and prices decide a farmer's income. A phone can now help with all three, often by voice in your own language. The Government runs several free tools for farmers. The big free AI chat apps, such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot and Meta AI in WhatsApp, can also explain things in simple words. Use them as a first helper. Before you spray, borrow or sell, check with your local agriculture officer or the Kisan Call Centre as well.

For a sick crop, start with a clear photo. The National Pest Surveillance System (NPSS), launched in 2024, has a mobile app and a website where you can upload photos of the pest or the damaged plant. It uses AI to identify the problem and gives crop protection advice. By December 2025 it covered 66 crops and more than 432 pests, and over 10,000 extension workers were using it. Show the result to your agriculture officer before you buy any pesticide.

For weather, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) updates its crop advisories for each district every Tuesday and Friday on imdagrimet.gov.in. Its Meghdoot app gives weather-based farm advice, and forecasts now go down to the gram panchayat through Mausamgram. For prices, eNAM (enam.gov.in) links 1,656 mandis in 23 states and 4 Union Territories. Its app shows free price information for 247 commodities, and the website can be read in 13 languages. Compare rates before you agree a price with a trader.

For scheme questions, Kisan e-Mitra is a Government voice chatbot. It answers questions on PM-KISAN, Kisan Credit Card and crop insurance (PMFBY) in 11 languages, more than 8,000 times a day. In February 2026 the Agriculture Ministry also launched Bharat-VISTAAR. Dial 155261 from any phone, even a basic one, and an AI assistant gives crop, weather, mandi price and scheme information. It began in Hindi and English. To speak to a person, call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551, between 6 am and 10 pm.

You can also talk to a general AI chat app. Google says Gemini's features work in 10 Indian languages, and the other big free apps can listen and reply in Hindi and many Indian languages too. Tap the microphone, say your district, crop, the crop's age and what you see, and ask for simple steps. But these apps do not know your soil, your local weather or which products are approved for your crop. They can name the wrong pest or the wrong dose. Take the answer to an expert.

Stay safe. Fake "PM Kisan" app files are sent on WhatsApp. In June 2025 Rajasthan Police warned that such a file gives criminals control of the phone, and they then use OTPs and banking apps to take money. Register for PM-KISAN only at pmkisan.gov.in, a Common Service Centre or the agriculture office, and install apps only from the Play Store. Never share an OTP or Aadhaar number with a caller. Report fraud on 1930. Before any spray, read the dose on the product label.
tips: Take a clear daylight photo of the damaged leaf and of the pest, then upload it in the NPSS app or show it to your agriculture officer.

Say to an AI app: "I grow cotton in Yavatmal district. The crop is 60 days old. The leaves are curling and there are white insects under them. What could it be, and what should I ask my agriculture officer?"
Check IMD's crop advisory for your district on Tuesday and Friday before you sow, spray or harvest.
Compare today's prices in two or three nearby mandis on eNAM before you sell.
Dial 155261 to ask Bharat-VISTAAR a question by voice, or call 1800-180-1551 to speak to a Kisan Call Centre expert.
Say: "Explain the PM Fasal Bima Yojana in simple Marathi. Which papers will the bank ask me for?" Then confirm the answer at your bank or Common Service Centre.
Never install an app file sent on WhatsApp, even if it carries a scheme name. Use only the Play Store.
If AI advice does not match what you see in your field, trust your eyes and ask a person you know.

guides.title: AI for homemakers in India
guides.summary: Plan meals, festivals and the monthly budget, help with homework, learn a skill and earn from home with free AI apps, by voice in your own language. Know the family scams to watch for.

stats.label: a day spent on unpaid housework by women and girls who do it; men and boys who do it spend 88 minutes
stats.source: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Time Use Survey 2024 press note, 25 February 2025

stats.label: women in self-help groups, as stated by the Rural Development Minister in January 2026
stats.source: News On AIR (Akashvani), 25 January 2026

stats.label: lost to cyber fraud in India in 2025, across 28.15 lakh complaints
stats.source: Government figures reported by The Pioneer, 15 September 2026

body: Running a home is real work. In the Government's Time Use Survey 2024, women and girls who did unpaid housework spent about 289 minutes a day on it. Men and boys who did it spent 88 minutes. A free AI chat app such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot or Meta AI in WhatsApp can take over some of the planning and writing. You do not have to type. Most apps have a microphone button, and Google says Gemini Live can talk in more than 25 Indian languages and dialects.

Start with food. Tell the AI how many people eat at home, your weekly budget in rupees, the vegetables in season and what your family will not eat. Ask for a seven-day menu and one shopping list for the sabzi mandi and the kirana shop. For Diwali, Eid, Pongal or a family function, ask for a guest menu, the quantity for 20 people and a day-by-day work plan. AI does not know today's prices in your town, so check the cost yourself.

For money, type or read out your monthly income and expenses: rent, school fees, milk, gas cylinder, electricity, EMI and mobile recharge. Ask for a simple budget table and two or three places to save. Check every total with a calculator, because AI makes mistakes in sums. AI can also explain a confusing bill or form in your language. It can draft a complaint to a shop, a leave note for school or a letter to the housing society. Read each line before you send it.

For homework, use AI to understand the chapter yourself, then guide your child. ChatGPT is not meant for children under 13, and OpenAI says an adult should do the typing for younger children. For health, AI can explain a medical word or a test report and help you list questions for the doctor. It cannot examine anyone, and it can be wrong. The doctor decides the medicine and the dose. The Government's eSanjeevani service offers free consultations with a doctor from home.

AI can help you learn and earn. Ask it to practise spoken English with you for ten minutes a day, or to teach you computer basics. SWAYAM (swayam.gov.in) is the Government's online course platform. To sell pickles, snacks, tiffin or tailoring from home, ask AI for a cost sheet, a fair price and a WhatsApp message for customers. About 10 crore women are in self-help groups, which can get bank loans. Since April 2026, home kitchens with turnover up to ₹1.5 crore need only basic FSSAI registration.

Stay safe. Never give a chatbot your Aadhaar, bank or card details, UPI PIN, OTP or passwords. Scams come by call, SMS and WhatsApp: a warning that your electricity or gas will be cut, a KYC update link, or an app file (APK) to install. The Home Ministry says install apps only from a trusted app store. A crying voice asking for money can be an AI copy, so call back on your saved number. If money is lost, call 1930. AI can also sound sure and be wrong.
tips: Say or type: "Plan 7 days of vegetarian lunch and dinner for 4 people in ₹2,000. Use vegetables that are in season now. Give me one shopping list."
Say: "I have leftover rice, two potatoes, curd and onions. Give me three quick recipes."
Say: "We have 25 guests for Diwali dinner. Suggest a simple menu, the quantity of each dish and what I can cook one day before."
Type: "My family income is ₹30,000 a month. These are my expenses: [list]. Make a budget table and show where I can save ₹2,000." Then check the totals with a calculator.
Type: "Explain fractions for Class 5 in simple Hindi so that I can teach my child. Then give 5 practice sums."

body: More women in India now run their own work, from a tiffin service or tailoring unit at home to a self-help group (SHG) that makes pickles, papad or bags. By February 2026, more than 3.07 crore women-led enterprises were registered on the Government's Udyam platforms. A free AI chat app such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot or Meta AI in WhatsApp can work like a business helper that is free at any hour. You can type, or speak in your own language.

Start with price. Tell the AI the cost of raw material, packing, transport, gas or power and your own time for one batch, and how many pieces you make. Ask for the cost per piece and a selling price with a fair profit. Then compare it with shop prices near you. For labels, ask what a pack should show, and check the answer with the rules. For food, FSSAI registration now covers businesses with a turnover up to ₹1.5 crore, and since April 2026 it does not need renewal.

For selling, ask the AI for short posts for WhatsApp Status, Instagram or Facebook, in your language and in English. Give real facts: ingredients, size, price and delivery area. Ask for five ideas for photos you can take at home in daylight. Ask for polite replies to common questions, such as "Do you take cash on delivery?" SHG products can also be listed on eSARAS (esaras.in), the official marketplace of DAY-NRLM. It is linked to ONDC and reaches buyers through more than 11 shopping apps.

For a loan, AI can help you write, not decide. Ask it to turn your notes into a one-page plan for the bank: what you make, monthly cost, monthly sales and what the loan will buy. Mudra loans need no collateral. They start with Shishu, up to ₹50,000, and go up to ₹20 lakh. Banks, small finance banks and microfinance lenders give them, and about 60% of Mudra loan accounts are held by women. Ask the lender for the real interest rate and terms.

Know the programmes. Under DAY-NRLM, about 10.13 crore women are members of 94.40 lakh SHGs. A Lakhpati Didi is an SHG member whose household earns at least ₹1 lakh a year; the official portal shows 3.76 crore, and the target is 6 crore by March 2029. Udyam registration is free. On GeM, the Womaniya section lets women-led enterprises and SHGs sell to government offices. For accounts, speak the day's sales and costs each evening and ask the AI for a simple weekly table.

Stay careful. AI can get sums, rules and scheme details wrong, so check with your bank, Common Service Centre, SHG federation or a CA. Any message offering a Mudra loan for a small fee is a scam. In July 2026 the Government called a letter fake that promised a ₹5 lakh Mudra loan for a ₹350 processing fee. Do not share Aadhaar, bank or OTP details. You never need to enter your UPI PIN to receive money. Keep your home address off public posts. Report fraud on 1930.
tips: Say: "I make mango pickle at home. One batch costs ₹1,800 for material, ₹300 for jars and ₹200 for gas, and gives 20 jars of 500 grams. What is my cost per jar? Suggest a selling price with 30% profit."
Type: "Write 3 short WhatsApp Status posts in Tamil and English for my home tailoring work. I stitch blouses and school uniforms. Delivery in 3 days."
Type: "List what the label of a packed food item should show. I will check it with the FSSAI rules."
Type: "Turn these notes into a one-page business plan for a bank loan: [what you make, monthly cost, monthly sales, loan amount, what you will buy]. Do not add numbers I have not given."
Say: "Explain in simple Hindi the difference between a Shishu and a Kishor Mudra loan. What questions should I ask the bank?"
Say each evening: "Today I sold [items] for Rs [amount] and spent Rs [amount] on [items]. Add this to my weekly account table."
Ask your SHG federation or block office how to list your products on eSARAS and on GeM Womaniya.
If anyone asks for a fee to approve a loan or a scheme, stop and call 1930.

body: India has about 1.03 crore school teachers and 24.72 crore students. On average there is one teacher for every 24 students, but more than one lakh schools still run with a single teacher. Planning, checking notebooks and paperwork take time away from teaching. A free AI chat app such as ChatGPT, Gemini or Copilot can prepare a first draft in minutes. You then correct it, because you know your students and your syllabus better than any app does.

Give the AI exact details: board, class, subject, chapter, period length and what you have in the classroom. Ask for a 40-minute lesson plan with one activity that uses everyday objects. Ask for a worksheet at three levels with an answer key, or a question paper with marks for each question. CBSE puts sample papers and marking schemes for Classes 10 and 12 on cbseacademic.nic.in. Paste your board's pattern and ask the AI to follow it.

AI helps where children speak one language at home and study in another. Ask it to explain a topic in simple Hindi or your state's language, with the English terms in brackets, or to make a two-language word list. If you are not fluent in it, ask a colleague to check. For a large class, ask for an activity that groups of six can do with one sheet of paper. For parents, ask for a polite WhatsApp message about a meeting or unfinished homework, then check the tone yourself.

Official platforms and training can help you. DIKSHA (diksha.gov.in) has curriculum-linked content for NCERT, CBSE, NIOS and state boards, and NISHTHA training courses for teachers. The Government's Skilling for AI Readiness (SOAR) programme has a 45-hour module called AI for Educators. In 2026-27 CBSE started a Computational Thinking and AI curriculum for Classes 3 to 8, with a teachers' handbook, and made it the year's training theme. The free YUVA AI for All course, a little over four hours long, is on DIKSHA and iGOT Karmayogi.

Students use AI too, so set clear rules. Say which tasks allow AI and which do not. Ask to see rough work, or ask two or three oral questions about the answer. Do not punish a child only because an "AI detector" gave a high score. OpenAI withdrew its own detector in 2023. It caught only 26% of AI-written text, wrongly flagged 9% of human writing, and worked much worse in languages other than English.

Stay careful. AI makes mistakes in facts, sums and answer keys, and may not match your state syllabus, so check every line before it reaches students. You decide the marks, not the app. Do not paste students' names, photos, marks, Aadhaar numbers or health details into a public AI app. India's data protection rules give children's data special protection, with a parent's consent needed in many cases. Follow your school's and board's rules, and ask your head teacher when you are unsure.
tips: Type: "Make a 40-minute lesson plan on fractions for Class 6, state board, 50 students. I have only a blackboard and chalk. Include one activity with paper strips."
Type: "Write 10 questions on this chapter: 4 easy, 4 medium and 2 hard, with marks and an answer key. Follow this pattern: [paste your board's pattern]."
Type: "Explain the water cycle in simple Hindi for Class 5, with the English terms in brackets."
Type: "Give me the same worksheet in an easier version and a harder version."
Type: "Write a short, polite WhatsApp message in Telugu and English inviting parents to a meeting on Saturday at 10 am."
Check every fact, sum and answer key yourself before you give it to the class.
Remove names, roll numbers and marks before you paste any student's work into an AI app.
Never decide a copying case on an AI detector score alone; talk to the student first.

guides.title: AI for office workers in India
guides.summary: Write emails and reports faster, get help with Excel, meetings and presentations, and improve your office English. Learn how to do this without putting company or customer data at risk.

body: AI is now common in Indian offices. In Microsoft's 2026 Work Trend Index, 87% of AI users in India said they stay responsible for the thinking and treat AI output only as a starting point. Infosys, TCS, Wipro and LTM have together signed up for more than 4 lakh Copilot licences. Whether you work in a bank branch, a factory office or a call centre, the free apps such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Copilot can all help with daily writing and number work.

Begin with writing. Type your points in rough English, or in Hindi and English mixed, and ask for a clear, polite email. Ask for three subject lines. For a report, give the facts and ask for a one-page summary with headings. If English is your second language, ask the AI to correct your draft and explain each change, so that you learn from it. Tell it to keep your meaning and not add new facts. Read the final text once before you send it.

For Excel or Google Sheets, describe your columns in words, for example: column A has branch, B has month, C has sales in rupees. Ask for the formula for total sales by branch, or for the steps to make a pivot table. Paste an error such as #N/A and ask what it means. Use made-up sample rows, not real customer data. Then test the result on a few rows with a calculator, and check that lakh and crore figures are shown the way your office writes them.

For meetings, paste your own rough notes and ask for a table of decisions, action points, owners and dates. For a presentation, ask for a six-slide outline with one message per slide, then put in the numbers yourself. For a customer complaint, describe the problem without the customer's name or account number. Ask for a calm reply that says sorry, explains the next step and gives a time. Record or transcribe a meeting only if your company allows it and everyone in the meeting agrees.

Follow your company's rules first. In January 2025 the Finance Ministry told its staff to avoid AI apps such as ChatGPT on office devices, to protect government data. In March 2025 CERT-In, the national cyber security agency, advised people not to use online AI tools for professional work that involves sensitive information. India's Digital Personal Data Protection Rules were notified on 14 November 2025, and the main duties for organisations are due from May 2027. The highest penalty, for failing to keep personal data safe, is ₹250 crore.

AI can be wrong and sound confident. In January 2026 the Bombay High Court ordered ₹50,000 in costs after a submission relied on a judgment the court could not trace. The judge said AI may be used for research, but every reference must be checked. The same rule fits office work. Check each number, name, date and rule against the original file. Do not paste salaries, customer lists, contracts or passwords into a public AI app. Your name is on the work, so you are responsible for it.
tips: Type: "Rewrite this email in simple, polite English. Keep my meaning. Then list the changes you made and why."
Type: "Column A has branch, B has month, C has sales in rupees. Give me an Excel formula for the total sales of each branch, and explain it step by step."
Type: "Turn these meeting notes into a table with four columns: decision, action, owner, date."
Type: "Make a 6-slide outline for a 10-minute presentation to my manager on [topic]. One main message per slide."
Type: "Write a calm reply to a customer whose refund is late. Say sorry, explain the next step and give a time. Keep it under 100 words."
Read your company's AI and IT policy, and use only the AI tools your employer has approved for work files.
Replace real names, phone numbers, account numbers and prices with made-up ones before you paste anything.
Check every number, date and rule in an AI draft against the original document before you send it.

body: Delivery riders, cab and auto drivers and other app-based workers spend the day on the road, with little time for paperwork. A free AI chat app such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot or Meta AI in WhatsApp can help in the gaps between orders. You can speak to it in Hindi, Tamil, Bengali or your own language, and it will answer in simple words. It can explain a rule, write a complaint, teach you English and add up your costs. It cannot see inside your platform account.

Start with your own app. Copy the text of a new rule, incentive plan or weekly pay statement, remove your phone number and ID, and ask: "Explain this in simple Hindi. What do I earn per order, and what is cut?" If your ID is blocked or a payment is short, tell the AI the dates, the order numbers and what happened. Ask for a short, polite complaint in English for the app's help section. Keep screenshots. If there is no reply, ask for a second, firmer letter.

Track your real income. Each night, say what you earned and what you spent on fuel or charging, EMI, repairs, phone recharge and food. Ask for a weekly table and your earning per hour after costs. For routes, use your maps app; a chat app does not know live traffic. In waiting time, practise English. Ask the AI to play a customer or a security guard and to correct you gently. Ask for five new sentences a day, or for help to learn a new skill.

Before a vehicle loan, give the AI the lender's figures and ask it to explain the EMI, interest rate, fees and the total you will repay. Mudra loans from banks cover commercial vehicles such as auto rickshaws and e-rickshaws. For insurance, ask what "third-party", "own damage" and "personal accident" mean. The Centre's 2025 ride-app guidelines say drivers who own the vehicle should get at least 80% of the fare, and all drivers ₹5 lakh health cover. In November 2026 the Transport Minister said only two states had adopted them.

Know where the law stands. The Code on Social Security recognises gig and platform workers. Register on the e-Shram portal (eshram.gov.in); it is free, and about 11.5 lakh platform workers had registered by August 2026. Central rules notified in May 2026 say you qualify for schemes after 90 days of work with one platform in a year, or 120 days across platforms. Karnataka and Telangana make platforms pay a welfare fee for workers. Rajasthan passed a law in 2023, but its rules were still pending at the end of 2025.

Stay careful. AI can be wrong about your platform's rules, labour law and loan terms, and it may invent a rule that sounds real. Check with the app's help section, your union or the labour office. Drivers are a target for fake e-challan messages. In September 2026 Kerala police warned of SMS links that install a harmful app file and take over the phone. Check challans only on the official Parivahan or e-challan website. Never pay an agent a joining fee, and never share your OTP. Report fraud on 1930.
tips: Type: "Explain this incentive rule in simple Hindi. How many orders do I need, and what do I lose if I cancel one? [paste the rule]"

Type: "My ID was blocked on [date] without a reason. I have completed [number] orders and my rating is [rating]. Write a short, polite appeal in English asking for the reason and for my ID to be restored."
Say each night: "Today I earned Rs [amount] in [number] hours. Fuel Rs [amount], food Rs [amount]. Add this to my weekly table and tell me my earning per hour after costs."
Say: "Act as a customer who cannot find my location. Speak in simple English. Correct my mistakes after each reply."
Type: "A lender offers Rs [amount] for [number] months at [rate]% interest with a fee of Rs [amount]. What is the EMI and the total I will repay? What should I ask the lender?"
Register free on eshram.gov.in or at a Common Service Centre, and ask there about PMSBY accident cover of ₹2 lakh.
Remove your phone number, ID number and bank details before you paste a pay statement into an AI app.
Do not open links in challan or KYC messages; type the official website address yourself.

body: India has an estimated 64.66 lakh handloom and handicraft artisans, and women are 71% of handloom weavers. Many more people earn as potters, tailors, carpenters, toy makers and metal workers. The skill is in your hands. The hard part is often words, photos and finding buyers. A free AI chat app such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot or Meta AI in WhatsApp can help, by typing or by voice in your own language. In 2026 the MSME Ministry trained over 2,500 PM Vishwakarma artisans to use such tools.

Tell the AI what only you know: the material, the technique, how many days one piece takes, your village or town, and how to care for the product. Ask for a short description for buyers, in English and Hindi. Do not let it add claims such as "pure silk" or "natural dye" unless they are true. For photos, use daylight and a plain background, with one full picture and one close-up. For price, add material, your days of labour, packing and courier, then ask for a fair price.

To sell beyond your town, look at Indiahandmade (indiahandmade.com), the Government's online marketplace for handloom and handicraft, built under the Ministry of Textiles. Sellers without GST registration can join with an Enrolment ID and sell within their own state. ONDC is another Government-backed selling network. For buyers in other states or abroad, ask the AI to translate messages and to explain courier and customs words. India Post has more than 1,000 Dak Ghar Niryat Kendras that help small sellers send export parcels.

PM Vishwakarma supports 18 traditional trades, such as carpenter, potter, tailor, cobbler, goldsmith, blacksmith, basket maker and toy maker. It gives an ID card, training with a stipend of ₹500 a day, ₹15,000 for tools, and loans without collateral of ₹1 lakh and then ₹2 lakh at 5% interest. The target of 30 lakh registrations is full, so ask a Common Service Centre if new ones are open. Handicraft artisans can also enrol under Pehchan with the Development Commissioner (Handicrafts).

Use AI for ideas, not for copying. Ask for new colour combinations or products based on your own craft, such as a laptop sleeve in your weave. Do not ask it to copy another maker or a brand. To protect your own new design, design registration lasts 10 years and can be extended by 5, but the design must not be published before you apply. A GI tag protects a region's craft, such as the Banarasi saree; a producers' group applies for it. A registered agent can guide you.

Stay careful. AI can write a wrong fibre name, size or care step, and its translation can sound odd, so ask someone who knows the language to read important messages. Watch for fake buyers. In July 2026 PhonePe warned about callers who pose as army men, send a QR code or payment request and ask for your UPI PIN. You never need a PIN to receive money. Take full or part payment before you ship. Do not pay anyone a fee to register for a scheme. Report fraud on 1930.

Before you post a new design online, ask about design registration; it must not be published before you apply.

body: Frontline health work is mostly talking and writing. An ASHA explains danger signs to a new mother. An ANM fills registers. A nurse or pharmacist explains how to take a medicine. A free AI chat app can help with the words. ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, Claude and Meta AI in WhatsApp can all turn hard medical language into simple words, and most work in Hindi and other big Indian languages. You remain the trained person. The app only helps you write, explain and learn.

Start with explaining. First read what the doctor or your programme guideline says. Then ask the AI to put that same message in simple words: short sentences, no medical terms, in the patient's language. Ask for a version you can read aloud, or for a simple example from village life. You can speak your request instead of typing. Google says Gemini Live can now talk in over 25 Indian languages and dialects. If you do not know the language well, ask a colleague who does to check it.

AI also saves writing time. Speak or type your rough points and ask for a neat monthly report, a short referral note or a meeting record. Leave out the patient's name and add it by hand on paper. For a health talk at a mothers' meeting, an Anganwadi centre or a school, ask for a ten-minute talk with three key messages and questions to ask the group. For revision, paste a page from your training module and ask for a quiz, one question at a time.

Use the official tools for patient care. eSanjeevani (esanjeevani.mohfw.gov.in), the national telemedicine service, has crossed 50 crore consultations and works in 15 languages. It links health centres and patients to doctors, and has an AI tool that supports the doctor during the consultation. Under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, over 93 crore ABHA accounts have been created. An ABHA is a 14-digit health ID, and records are shared only with the patient's consent. Patient details belong in these systems, not in a chat app.

India's health programmes also use official AI tools. The Health Ministry has reported Cough against TB for TB screening in the community, DeepCXR for reading chest X-rays, and MadhuNetrAI, which grades eye photos taken by non-specialist health workers to find diabetic eye disease. These tools help with screening and referral. They support trained staff and do not replace them. In February 2026 the Ministry released SAHI, a national framework for safe and ethical AI in health care. The Government says its health AI tools follow ICMR's 2023 ethical guidelines.

AI must not diagnose, choose a treatment or decide a dose. It can sound sure and still be wrong. Even OpenAI's rules do not allow tailored advice that needs a licence unless a licensed professional is involved. CERT-In, India's cyber security agency, advises people not to rely on AI for medical decisions. Check every medicine fact against the prescription or your programme guideline, and ask the doctor when unsure. Never put a patient's name, phone number, Aadhaar or ABHA number, report or photo into a public AI app.
tips: Say or type: "Explain anaemia in pregnancy to a village woman in simple Marathi. Use short sentences and no medical words. I will read it aloud."
Type: "These are the doctor's instructions: [paste them without the name]. Rewrite only these in simple Hindi. Do not add or change any medicine or dose."
Type: "Turn my rough notes into a short referral note with these headings: complaint, findings, what was done, reason for referral." Add the patient's name by hand.
Type: "Write a 10-minute health talk on handwashing for mothers at an Anganwadi centre, in simple Telugu, with 3 key messages and 3 questions to ask the group."
Paste a page from your training module and type: "Ask me 10 quiz questions on this page, one at a time, and tell me if I am right."
In a small clinic, type: "Write a one-page patient handout on foot care in diabetes, in simple Kannada and English." Read and correct it before you print.
Describe a case as "a 30-year-old pregnant woman", never by name; Google says human reviewers may read some Gemini chats.
When a patient needs a doctor's opinion, use eSanjeevani at your health centre or refer; do not ask a chat app to decide.

guides.title: AI for senior citizens in India
guides.summary: Use AI by voice in your own language to understand a prescription, a pension form or a bank letter, and to stay in touch with family. Know the scams that target senior citizens and where to get help.

stats.label: people aged 60 and above expected in India by 2036, about 15% of the population
stats.source: Press Information Bureau, Elderly in India backgrounder, 28 October 2025

stats.label: digital life certificates submitted by pensioners through Jeevan Pramaan since 2014
stats.source: Jeevan Pramaan portal, Government of India, viewed 25 November 2026

stats.label: Elderline, the toll-free national helpline for senior citizens, open 8 am to 8 pm every day
stats.source: Manorama Yearbook, on the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment helpline, 16 July 2026

body: You do not need to type or know English to use AI. Open a free app such as ChatGPT or Gemini, or Meta AI inside WhatsApp. Tap the microphone button and speak as you would to a helpful neighbour. Google says Gemini Live can talk in more than 25 Indian languages and dialects, including Bhojpuri and Maithili. Ask it to speak slowly, to repeat, or to use simpler words. A family member can set up the app once. Then ask about a news item, a recipe or a hard word.

Before a doctor visit, AI can help you understand, not decide. Take a clear photo of a prescription or lab report, or read it out, and ask what each word means in your language. It can misread handwriting and numbers, so never start, stop or change a medicine because an app said so. Cover your name and phone number in the photo. Everyone aged 70 and above can get free hospital treatment of up to ₹5 lakh a year under Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY.

Pensioners must submit a life certificate to keep the pension coming. Jeevan Pramaan is the Government's digital life certificate. You can make it at home with face authentication on a smartphone, at a bank or Common Service Centre, or through the postman. India Post Payments Bank charges ₹70 for each certificate and nothing extra for the home visit. In November 2026 the Government ran its fifth nationwide campaign to help pensioners do this. AI can explain a pension form or bank letter in simple words, but confirm the rule with your bank or pension office.

AI can help you stay close to family. Ask it to write a birthday blessing, a wedding wish or a message to a grandchild abroad, in your language or in English. Ask for the steps to make a WhatsApp video call, one step at a time. An app is not a person, though. If you feel lonely, or need guidance on pension, maintenance, care homes or ill-treatment, call Elderline on 14567. This toll-free national helpline for senior citizens is open from 8 am to 8 pm, seven days a week.

Scammers target senior citizens. In a "digital arrest" scam, someone on a video call pretends to be from the police, CBI, customs or a court and says you must pay to clear your name. Delhi Police said in October 2026 that there is no such thing as digital arrest in law, and that no police, CBI, RBI or court officer asks for money on a video call. Disconnect and tell your family. For a KYC update, RBI says contact your bank directly and never share an OTP, PIN or password.

Remember the limits. AI can sound sure and still be wrong about medicines, pension rules, dates and interest rates, so check with your doctor, bank or pension office. Do not say your Aadhaar number, bank details, PIN or OTP to a chatbot. A voice that sounds like your son or granddaughter asking for urgent money can be copied by AI. Hang up and call back on the number you have saved. If money has gone, call 1930 at once, inform your bank and report at cybercrime.gov.in.
tips: Tap the microphone and say: "Please answer in simple Marathi and speak slowly." Use your own language in place of Marathi.
Show a photo of your lab report and say: "Explain each test in simple Hindi. What should I ask my doctor?"
Say: "Write a short birthday blessing for my grandson in Tamil and in English."
Say: "Tell me the steps to make a WhatsApp video call, one step at a time. Wait until I say next."
Say: "Explain this bank letter in simple words. What do I have to do, and by which date?" Then confirm it at your branch.
Ask your family to help you submit your digital life certificate on time, or ask the postman about the doorstep service.
If a caller on video says you are under "digital arrest", disconnect, tell your family and call 1930.
Agree a secret family word. Anyone who phones for urgent money must say it first.

guides.title: AI for parents of young children in India
guides.summary: Know the age rules of the main AI apps, set safe limits and help with homework without copying. Know what Indian law says about children's data and where to report bullying or fake photos.

stats.label: the most screen time a day advised for children aged 2 to 5; none is advised below 2 years
stats.source: Indian Academy of Pediatrics, Screen Time Guidelines for Parents, 2021

stats.label: the age up to which India's data protection law treats a person as a child, whose data needs a parent's consent
stats.source: Observer Research Foundation, DPDP Rules and the future of child data safety, 20 November 2025

body: AI chat apps now sit inside phones, search and WhatsApp, but they were made for adults and teenagers. As checked in November 2026: ChatGPT is not meant for children under 13, and those aged 13 to 18 need a parent's permission. Gemini is for ages 13 and above, unless a parent turns it on for a younger child in Google Family Link. Meta AI in WhatsApp has a 13+ setting. Claude is only for adults aged 18 and above. Rules change, so read each app's help page.

Think about screen time first. The Indian Academy of Pediatrics advises no screens below the age of 2, except an occasional video call with relatives, and not more than one hour a day from 2 to 5 years. For older children, screens must not push out sleep, outdoor play, study, meals and family time. It suggests screen-free places such as the bedroom and the dining table, and switching screens off one hour before bed. Children copy their parents, so your own phone habits matter too.

For homework, sit together. For a child under 13, you type or speak, and you read the answer first. OpenAI says an adult should do this for young children. Ask AI to explain the idea in simple words in your language. Then let your child solve the sum or write the answer alone. Ask for five practice questions, a quiz on the chapter, or a story with your child as the hero. Copying an AI answer into the notebook teaches nothing, and the answer may be wrong.

Use the safety settings. In ChatGPT, a parent can link to a teenager's account under Settings, then Parental controls, to set quiet hours, turn off voice or image making and reduce sensitive content. Parents cannot read the chats. In Google Family Link you can switch Gemini on or off for your child. Since September 2026, WhatsApp lets parents choose a stricter "Limited Content" setting for Meta AI on a teenager's account. Google advises telling children that AI is a tool, not a person, and not a place for secrets.

Indian law treats everyone under 18 as a child for personal data. Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act and the Rules notified in November 2025, apps must get a parent's verifiable consent before using a child's data. They must not track children or aim advertisements at them. These duties are due to begin in May 2027 and were not yet in force in late 2026. Since February 2026, IT rules also require AI-made photos, audio and videos to carry a clear label.

If someone bullies your child online or shares a fake or morphed photo, stay calm and tell your child it is not their fault. Do not reply to the bully. Save screenshots, block the sender and report the account in the app. Under the 2026 IT rules, a platform must remove nude, sexual or morphed images within two hours of a complaint. Report at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930. Child Helpline 1098 is free and open 24 hours; call 112 in an emergency. AI also makes mistakes, so stay nearby.
tips: For a child under 13, sit side by side: your child asks, you type or speak, and you read the answer first.
Say: "Explain why the moon changes shape, for a 7-year-old, in simple Hindi. Then ask three easy questions."
Say: "Tell a short bedtime story about [your child's name] and a clever parrot in a village. Stop twice and let us choose what happens next."
Type: "Do not give the answer. Give my child one small hint at a time for this sum: [sum]."
Teach three rules: AI is a tool, not a friend; it can be wrong; never tell it your name, school, address or send your photo.
Keep phones out of the bedroom and off the dining table, and switch screens off one hour before sleep.
If your teenager uses ChatGPT, link the accounts under Settings, then Parental controls, and set quiet hours for the night.
If a fake or hurtful photo appears, save screenshots, block the sender, report it in the app, then report at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930 or 1098.

guides.title: AI for girls and young women in India
guides.summary: Use AI to plan studies and a career, find scholarships, return to work, practise interviews and start something of your own. Know exactly where to report a fake or morphed photo.

stats.label: a year from AICTE's Pragati scholarship for girls in technical degree and diploma courses; 10,000 are given each year
stats.source: All India Council for Technical Education, Students Development Schemes page, viewed 25 November 2026

stats.label: fee for Udyam registration of a small business on the official portal; no private agency is authorised to do it
stats.source: Udyam Registration portal, Ministry of MSME, viewed 25 November 2026

stats.label: time a platform has to remove nude, sexual or morphed images after a complaint, under IT rules in force from 20 February 2026
stats.source: Chambers and Partners, note on the IT Amendment Rules, 2026

body: A free AI chat app can be a patient study partner and career guide. ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot and Meta AI can all explain a subject, compare courses, improve a CV and practise interviews. You can type or speak, in your own language or in English. Use it to ask the questions you cannot easily ask at home or in class, at any hour. Then check the important answers on official websites, because AI can be wrong and still sound sure. The choices about your studies, work and money stay yours.

For career planning, tell the AI your class or degree, your marks, the subjects you like, your town and what your family can spend. Ask for five career paths, with the course, entrance exam, years of study and first job for each. Ask what a nurse, a chartered accountant, a data analyst or a police officer does all day. Then check fees and admission dates on the college's own website. AI does not know this year's cut-offs, and it sometimes names colleges or courses that do not exist.

Money need not stop your studies. The National Scholarship Portal (scholarships.gov.in) lists Government scholarships in one place. AICTE's Pragati scholarship gives ₹50,000 a year to girls in technical degree and diploma courses, with 10,000 awards each year. For 2026-27, applications for Pragati, the college scholarship under PM-USP and the National Scholarship for Post Graduate Studies were open on the portal until the end of November 2026. Dates change every year, so read the portal itself. AI can explain the rules and list the documents, but only you can apply.

If you are returning to work after marriage, a child or caring for parents, AI can help you explain the gap honestly. List what you did in those years, such as managing the home budget, tutoring or helping in a family shop. Ask AI to put it in CV words without adding anything false. Practise interviews aloud: ask it to act as the HR person and to ask about the salary you expect. The National Career Service (ncs.gov.in) is free and has a Jobs for Women section.

To start something of your own, ask AI for a one-page plan: what you will sell, the cost of each item, the price, and how many you must sell each month to cover costs. Ask for a name and a short WhatsApp or Instagram message. Udyam registration for a small business is free and paperless on udyamregistration.gov.in. Mudra loans need no collateral, and the smallest, Shishu, is up to ₹50,000. Ask a bank for the full terms before you borrow.

Your safety online matters. Anyone can misuse a photo to make a fake or morphed image; the wrong is theirs, not yours. Do not pay, and do not send more pictures. Save screenshots and report the account. Under India's 2026 IT rules, a platform must remove nude, sexual or morphed images within two hours of a complaint. Report at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930. For support, call the women's helpline 181 or the NCW helpline 14490, and 112 in an emergency. Never give a chatbot your address, passwords or private photos.
tips: Type: "I am in Class 12 with Biology, in a small town in Bihar. My family can spend ₹60,000 a year. Suggest 5 career paths with the course, entrance exam and years of study."
Type: "Explain the rules of this scholarship in simple Hindi and list the documents I need: [paste the rules from scholarships.gov.in]."
Type: "I took a 6-year break to raise my child. This is what I did in those years: [list]. Write 3 honest lines for my CV."
Say: "Act as an HR interviewer for an office assistant job. Ask one question at a time, including my expected salary. Then tell me how to answer better."
Type: "I want to sell hand-embroidered dupattas. Each one costs me ₹350 to make. Help me set a price and work out how many I must sell to earn ₹10,000 a month."
If anyone threatens to share a real or fake photo of you: do not pay, save screenshots, report in the app, then report at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930.
To stop an intimate image spreading, use takeitdown.ncmec.org if you were under 18 in it, or StopNCII.org if you were an adult; the picture stays on your phone.
For sexual harassment at work, any woman can file a complaint on the Government's SHe-Box portal (shebox.wcd.gov.in).

guides.summary: Use free phone tools and AI apps to read text aloud, describe photos, caption speech, simplify wording and write applications, in Indian languages. Know the official support that is live now.

stats.label: Unique Disability ID (UDID) cards generated in India (1,34,73,833)
stats.source: Press Information Bureau, Bridging Digital Divide backgrounder, 8 March 2026

stats.label: kinds of disability covered by the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 and the UDID card
stats.source: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, UDID page, updated 11 June 2026

body: A phone with AI can read, describe, listen and write for you, in private and at your own speed. About 1.35 crore Unique Disability ID (UDID) cards have been issued in India. ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot and Meta AI all work by voice as well as typing. Google says Gemini Live can talk in over 25 Indian languages and dialects. On Android, the TalkBack screen reader supports Hindi, Bangla, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Punjabi, Tamil and Telugu, though not on every phone. You choose which tools suit you.

If you are blind or have low vision, Google's Lookout app on Android reads printed text and full pages aloud, describes photos and tells you the value of Indian rupee notes, though not coins. Its language list includes Hindi, Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Marathi, Tamil and Telugu, but detailed image descriptions are in English only. You can also give a photo to an AI chat app and ask what it shows. Sugamya Pustakalaya (sugamyapustakalaya.org.in) is the Government's online library of accessible books for people who cannot read print.

If you are Deaf or hard of hearing, Live Caption on Android adds captions to videos, calls and voice messages. Google says the captions are made on the phone and never leave it. Hindi works on Pixel and some other phones. AI chat apps can also turn a long written message into short, clear points. For Indian Sign Language, ISLRTC (islrtc.nic.in) offers a free online basic course, the Sign Learn app and NCERT books in ISL on DIKSHA. It has made more than 3,000 learning videos in ISL.

If reading, learning or attention is difficult, AI can make a page easier. Paste a long notice, a school circular or a bank letter and ask for five short points in simple words, in your language. Ask it to explain one line at a time, or to read its answer aloud. Ask it to break a big task, such as filling in a scholarship form, into small steps you can tick off. If typing is hard, speak. If speaking is hard, type. Ask again as often as you need.

AI is useful for applications. Give it the facts and ask for a short, polite letter: a request to your college for a scribe, a ramp at your office, or a complaint to a grievance officer. The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 covers 21 disabilities. It reserves 4% of government jobs and at least 5% of seats in government colleges for people with 40% disability or more. Apply for the UDID card at swavlambancard.gov.in. The National Scholarship Portal lists scholarships for students with disabilities, including AICTE's Saksham.

Know the limits. AI can misread a medicine label, a bus number or a rupee note. Google says poor light, blur or a covered object can spoil Lookout's results. For medicine doses, crossing a road or signing a paper, ask a person you trust. Captions can miss or change words. A photo you send to a chat app leaves your phone, so do not photograph Aadhaar, UDID or bank cards unless you must. Check rules about benefits with the district office or the official website, not only with a chatbot.
tips: Open Lookout, choose Currency and hold one note in front of the camera to hear its value.
Send a photo to an AI app and say: "Describe this photo in Hindi. Read out any text you can see."
Press a volume button on an Android phone, then turn on Live Caption under the volume controls and try it on a video.
Type: "Rewrite this notice in very simple Marathi. Use short sentences. Give me only the 5 most important points."
Type: "Break this task into small steps with a time for each: filling in my scholarship form."
Type: "Write a polite application to my college principal asking for a scribe and extra time in the exam. I have low vision and hold a UDID card. Keep it under 150 words."
Apply for your UDID card only on swavlambancard.gov.in, and look for scholarships on scholarships.gov.in.
Never rely on AI alone for medicine names, doses or expiry dates; ask a person to check.

guides.title: AI for government schemes, forms and complaints
guides.summary: Use AI to understand a scheme, list the documents you need, draft an application, RTI or complaint, and turn an official notice into simple words in your language. Then finish the work only on the official site or at an official centre.

stats.source: Press Information Bureau (PIB Research), digital infrastructure note, 12 August 2026

stats.label: registered DigiLocker users on 31 July 2026
stats.source: Press Information Bureau (PIB Research), digital infrastructure note, 12 August 2026

stats.source: Press Information Bureau (PIB Research), CPGRAMS note, 9 August 2026

body: Government work often means long forms and hard official language. A free AI chat app can help you understand and prepare. ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, Claude and Meta AI in WhatsApp can all explain a scheme, list likely documents, draft a letter and translate a notice into simple Hindi, Tamil or your own language. You can speak to it instead of typing. But a chat app is not the Government. It cannot apply for you, check your status or promise that you are eligible.

To find schemes, start on myScheme (myscheme.gov.in), the national scheme search platform. You enter basic details such as your age and occupation, and it shows Central and state schemes that may fit. Each scheme page gives the benefits, eligibility, documents needed and how to apply. If the page is hard to read, copy the text into an AI app and ask for simple points in your language. Treat anything the AI says about your eligibility as a guess until the office confirms it.

Keep documents and services on official apps. DigiLocker (digilocker.gov.in) stores digital copies of documents and certificates and has over 72 crore registered users. UMANG (web.umang.gov.in) brings 2,585 government services into one app and website. Ask AI to make a checklist of documents for your application and to explain each difficult word on the form. Do not type your Aadhaar number, bank account or passwords into the chat. Enter those yourself, only on the official form.

For a complaint about a government service, use CPGRAMS (pgportal.gov.in). Lodging a grievance is free, you get a registration number to track it, and the time limit to resolve it is 21 days. Since May 2026 its voice chatbot, Samadhan Didi, lets you speak your complaint in your own language. To ask a Central Government office for information, file an RTI at rtionline.gov.in. The fee is ₹10, with no fee for people below the poverty line. That portal is not for state offices; states have their own rules.

Use AI to draft, then check. Tell it the facts in order: what happened, when, which office, and what you want. Ask for a short, polite letter, or an RTI with clear numbered questions. The RTI portal allows 3,000 characters, so keep it brief. For a notice or bill, take a photo or paste the text, hide your ID numbers, and ask what it says, what you must do and by which date. The Government's Bhashini service (bhashini.gov.in) and app also translate text and speech in 22 Indian languages.

AI can give wrong eligibility rules, old dates and web addresses that do not exist, so check everything on the official site, usually ending in .gov.in or .nic.in. In September 2026 PIB Fact Check called videos of the Prime Minister on government schemes fake and AI-generated. Never pay an agent through a chat, and never share an OTP, Aadhaar number or bank details there. For help with a form, visit one of over 5 lakh Common Service Centres. Report fraud on 1930 or at cybercrime.gov.in.
tips: Paste a scheme page from myscheme.gov.in and say or type: "Explain this in simple Hindi: who can get it, what the benefit is, which documents are needed and where to apply."
Type: "Make a checklist of the documents I should carry for an income certificate, with one line on each. Tell me which points I must confirm with the office."
Type: "Write a short, polite complaint for CPGRAMS. Facts: [what happened, dates, office]. What I want: [action]. Do not add anything I have not told you."
Type: "Write an RTI application to [Central Government department] with 5 clear numbered questions about [subject]. Keep it under 3,000 characters."
Photograph a notice or bill, cover your account and ID numbers, and ask: "What does this say, what must I do, and what is the last date? Answer in simple Tamil."
Try the official chatbots: Samadhan Didi on CPGRAMS takes a complaint by voice, and Kisan e-Mitra answers farmers' questions on farm schemes.
Before you enter an OTP or pay a fee, read the web address and make sure it is the official one, such as pgportal.gov.in or rtionline.gov.in.
If a chat, call or video promises a scheme benefit for a fee, stop; check on myscheme.gov.in or at a Common Service Centre.

guides.title: AI for first-time users: start in your own language
guides.summary: Start using a free AI chat app by speaking in your own language, even if you do not read or type English. The first five tips are safe things to try today; the guide also covers what never to share and how to tell when AI is wrong.

body: An AI chat app is a computer program you can talk to like a helpful person. You ask a question by typing or speaking, and it answers in full sentences. It has learnt from a very large amount of writing, so it can explain, translate, write letters and answer follow-up questions. It is not a person, and it does not truly know things. It builds a likely answer, so it is sometimes wrong. Well-known apps are ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, Claude and Meta AI inside WhatsApp.

You can start for free. If you use WhatsApp, Meta AI may already be there as a chat. Gemini's basic plan costs ₹0 a month with a Google account, and ChatGPT also has a free plan. Install apps only from the Play Store or App Store, and check the maker's name. Free plans limit how much you can use each day, which is fine for learning. India has about 111 crore internet connections, and 44% of internet users already use AI features such as voice search.

You do not need to type or to know English. Tap the microphone and speak in Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Marathi or another language, or mix it with English. Google says Gemini Live can talk in over 25 Indian languages and dialects, and ChatGPT has Hindi voices. Some languages work better than others, so try yours. Ask the app to reply in your language and read the answer aloud. Then say: explain it like I am a beginner, with one example from daily life.

The camera helps a lot if reading is hard. In the app, tap the camera or plus button and take a photo of a signboard, a medicine label, an electricity bill or a letter. Then say: read this aloud and explain it in simple words in my language. Ask what you need to do and by which date. Cover your Aadhaar number, bank account number and any OTP before you take the photo. For important papers and medicines, ask a trusted person or a pharmacist to check too.

You can also learn more for free. The Government's YUVA AI for All course (futureskillsprime.in) is free, takes a little over four hours, needs no technical background and was announced in 11 Indian languages, with a Government of India certificate. An earlier rural scheme, PMGDISHA, trained 6.39 crore people in digital skills by March 2024. If you want a person to help you, more than 5 lakh Common Service Centres give assisted access to online services across the country.

Never tell a chat app your Aadhaar number, bank or card details, UPI PIN, passwords or any OTP. Google says human reviewers may read some Gemini chats, so do not share private things. AI can be wrong and still sound sure. Be most careful with numbers, dates, rules, phone numbers and web addresses. Ask it again in other words, and check with an official site or a person you trust. For health, legal or money matters, ask a qualified person. If you lose money to an online fraud, call 1930.
tips: Say: "Explain what a UPI PIN is and why I must keep it secret, like I am a beginner, in simple Hindi."
Say: "I have rice, dal, potatoes and onions. Suggest three simple dinners for four people."
Say: "Write a short, polite message in Marathi to my child's teacher. My son has fever and will miss school for two days."
Take a photo of a signboard, a label or a letter and say: "Read this aloud and explain it in simple Bengali."
Say: "Teach me five useful English sentences for talking to a bank officer. Say each one slowly and give the meaning in Tamil."
Test it: ask about something you know well, such as your own town or your trade, and notice where it is wrong.
Ask: "Are you sure? Which part should I check on an official site?" Then check it yourself.
Never say or type your Aadhaar number, bank details, UPI PIN, password or OTP, even if a chat asks for it.
